title: Revelation Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Revelation chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Revelation Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Revelation Chapter 17.

questions.question: In Revelation 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The woman is drunken with the blood of the saints
One of the seven angels with the seven vials talks with John
The woman sits upon a scarlet coloured beast
A name is written on the woman's forehead
questions.correctAnswer: One of the seven angels with the seven vials talks with John
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:1 states that one of the seven angels with the seven vials came and talked with John, which is the first event mentioned.

questions.question: Who came to talk with John in Revelation 17?
options: One of the seven angels which had the seven vials
questions.correctAnswer: One of the seven angels which had the seven vials
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:1 says that one of the seven angels which had the seven vials came and talked with John.

questions.question: According to Revelation 17, what judgment is shown to John?
options: The judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters
The judgment of the kings of the earth
The judgment of the seven heads
The judgment of the ten horns
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:1 states the angel will show John the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters.

questions.question: With whom have the kings of the earth committed fornication according to Revelation 17?
options: With the woman on the beast
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:2 states the kings of the earth have committed fornication with the great whore.

questions.question: What effect has the wine of the great whore's fornication had on the inhabitants of the earth?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:2 says the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication.

questions.question: Where was John carried by the spirit in Revelation 17?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 states he was carried away in the spirit into the wilderness.

questions.question: What color was the beast that the woman sat upon?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 describes the beast as scarlet coloured.

questions.question: How many heads did the beast have in Revelation 17?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 says the beast had seven heads.

questions.question: How many horns did the scarlet beast have?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 states the beast had ten horns.

questions.question: What colors was the woman arrayed in according to Revelation 17?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:4 says the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour.

questions.question: What did the woman hold in her hand?
options: A golden cup full of abominations and filthiness
A silver cup full of water
questions.correctAnswer: A golden cup full of abominations and filthiness
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:4 states she had a golden cup full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication.

questions.question: What name was written on the woman's forehead?
options: MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH
questions.correctAnswer: MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:5 states this exact name was written on her forehead.

questions.question: The woman was drunken with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus.
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:6 says the woman was drunken with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus.

questions.question: John wondered with great admiration when he saw the woman.
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:6 states John wondered with great admiration when he saw her.

questions.question: The text says the woman was riding a white horse.
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 says the woman sat upon a scarlet coloured beast, not a white horse.

medium.title: Revelation Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Revelation Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the angel reveal is a mystery concerning the woman and the beast?
options: The beast has seven heads and ten horns
questions.correctAnswer: The beast has seven heads and ten horns
questions.explanation: This is stated in Revelation 17:7, where the angel explains the mystery of the woman and the beast, emphasizing the beast's characteristics.

questions.question: What does Revelation 17:8 promise will happen to the beast that was and is not?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:8 states that the beast will ascend out of the bottomless pit and go into perdition, indicating its ultimate downfall.

questions.question: According to Revelation 17:9, what do the seven heads represent?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:9 explains that the seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits, symbolizing a specific connection.

questions.question: In Revelation 17:10, how many kings are mentioned, and what is notable about them?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:10 notes that there are seven kings, with five having fallen, indicating a historical progression among these rulers.

questions.question: What is the identity of the beast mentioned in Revelation 17:11?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:11 identifies the beast that was and is not as the eighth king, indicating its unique and powerful status.

questions.question: According to Revelation 17:12, what do the ten horns represent?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:12 clarifies that the ten horns are ten kings who have yet to receive a kingdom, suggesting an impending power shift.

questions.question: In Revelation 17:3, what does the woman sit upon?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:3 describes the woman sitting upon a scarlet coloured beast, which is significant to her identity and the narrative.

questions.question: What type of power do the ten kings receive according to Revelation 17:12?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:12 states that the ten kings will receive power as kings for one hour with the beast, highlighting the temporary nature of their authority.

questions.question: What does the woman in Revelation 17:4 hold in her hand?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:4 indicates that the woman has a golden cup in her hand, which is full of abominations and signifies her corrupt nature.

questions.question: According to Revelation 17:5, what is written on the woman's forehead?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:5 reveals the name written on the woman's forehead, emphasizing her identity and role in the prophetic narrative.

questions.question: In Revelation 17:6, what is the woman drunk with?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:6 states that the woman is drunken with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus, highlighting her violent and corrupt actions.

questions.question: What does the angel ask John in Revelation 17:7?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:7 contains the angel's question to John, prompting him to reflect on what he has seen and understood.

questions.question: True or False: The beast that carries the woman is described as having seven heads and ten horns.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Revelation 17:7 explicitly describes the beast as having seven heads and ten horns.

questions.question: True or False: The ten kings mentioned in Revelation 17:12 have already received their kingdoms.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Revelation 17:12 states that the ten kings have received no kingdom as yet.

questions.question: True or False: The woman in Revelation 17 is portrayed as a symbol of purity and righteousness.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as Revelation 17:4 and 17:6 depict the woman as corrupt, holding abominations and being drunk with the blood of saints.

hard.title: Revelation Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Revelation Chapter 17.

questions.question: What do the ten horns on the beast represent?
questions.explanation: The ten horns represent ten kings who have received no kingdom yet but will receive power as kings for a short time with the beast. This is found in Revelation 17:12.

questions.question: Who shall make war with the Lamb?
questions.explanation: It is stated in Revelation 17:14 that these shall make war with the Lamb, but the Lamb shall overcome them.

questions.question: What is the fate of the whore according to Revelation 17:16?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:16 describes how the ten horns shall hate the whore and make her desolate and naked.

questions.question: According to Revelation 17:18, what does the woman represent?
questions.explanation: The woman seen by John represents that great city which reigns over the kings of the earth, as stated in Revelation 17:18.

questions.question: Who are described as 'called, chosen, and faithful'?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:14 mentions that those who are with the Lamb are called, chosen, and faithful.

questions.question: What is the significance of the waters in Revelation 17:15?
questions.explanation: The waters where the whore sits symbolize peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues, as explained in Revelation 17:15.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'beast' in Revelation 17:12 mean?
questions.explanation: In Revelation 17:12, the Greek word for 'beast' (therion) translates to 'animal,' emphasizing its ferocity and destructive nature.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Revelation 17:14 with the phrase 'Lord of lords, and King of kings'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Lord of lords, and King of kings' is an example of parallelism, emphasizing the supremacy of Christ in Revelation 17:14.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the Lamb overcoming in Revelation 17:14?
questions.explanation: John 16:33 echoes the theme of overcoming, where Jesus states He has overcome the world, similar to the Lamb overcoming in Revelation 17:14.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the concept of God's will being fulfilled as seen in Revelation 17:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 14:24 states that the Lord's purpose will stand, fulfilling the theme of God's will being done found in Revelation 17:17.

questions.question: What comes before Revelation 17:14?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:14 directly follows Revelation 17:13, where it speaks of the ten horns giving their power to the beast.

questions.question: In Revelation 17:13, how do the ten kings relate to the beast?
options: They are afraid of the beast
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:13 describes that the ten kings have one mind and will give their power and strength unto the beast, indicating their support.

questions.question: The description of the woman in Revelation 17 includes being drunken with what?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:6 states that the woman was drunken with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: The whore is described as being adorned with gold and precious stones.
questions.explanation: True. Revelation 17:4 describes the woman as being arrayed in purple, scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones.

questions.question: True or False: The ten kings receive power as kings indefinitely.
questions.explanation: False. Revelation 17:12 states that the ten kings receive power for only one hour with the beast, indicating a limited time.

theological.title: Revelation Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Revelation Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 17:2 teach about human sin?
options: Human sin manifests corporately as idolatry and spiritual adultery with worldly powers
Human sin is primarily individual and unrelated to political alliances
Human sin is only about personal moral failures without social implications
Human sin is punished immediately without divine patience
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin manifests corporately as idolatry and spiritual adultery with worldly powers
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:2 describes the kings of the earth committing fornication with the woman, symbolizing corporate idolatry and alliance with evil powers, indicating a collective and spiritual adultery as a form of sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's victory over evil does Revelation 17:14 teach?
options: Christ as Lord of lords and King of kings will ultimately defeat all opposition
Christ will share power with earthly kings in the final battle
Christ's victory depends on human military strength
Christ will allow the beast to reign eternally
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as Lord of lords and King of kings will ultimately defeat all opposition
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:14 states the Lamb shall overcome those who make war with him, affirming Christ's sovereign and eternal victory over evil powers.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and perdition does Revelation 17:8 teach?
options: The beast is destined for final perdition after a period of apparent existence
The beast is immortal and will never be judged
The beast represents a righteous kingdom
The beast's power is independent of God's sovereign will
questions.correctAnswer: The beast is destined for final perdition after a period of apparent existence
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:8 explains the beast 'was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition,' emphasizing the temporal nature of evil and its destined judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 17:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:17 shows that God puts it into the hearts of the kings to fulfill His will, demonstrating His sovereign control over earthly powers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated by Revelation 17:7's angelic explanation of the mystery?
questions.explanation: In Revelation 17:7, the angel reveals the mystery of the woman and the beast, highlighting God's attribute of revealing hidden truth to His people.

questions.question: How does Revelation 17:5's depiction of 'Babylon the Great' connect to Old Testament prophetic themes?
options: It echoes the judgment on Babylon as a symbol of idolatry and oppression in Isaiah and Jeremiah
It introduces a new concept unrelated to OT prophecy
It primarily focuses on Israel's restoration
It symbolizes a literal city without theological meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the judgment on Babylon as a symbol of idolatry and oppression in Isaiah and Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:5 calls the woman 'Babylon the Great,' connecting her to the Old Testament symbolic use of Babylon as a representation of evil and idolatry, notably in Isaiah 13-14 and Jeremiah 50-51.

questions.question: In what way does Revelation 17:16's destruction of the harlot by the ten horns fulfill redemptive history?
options: It depicts the ultimate judgment and removal of corrupt worldly powers aligned against God
It shows the permanent alliance between evil powers
It endorses the harlot's continued influence
It suggests the ten horns fail to act against evil
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts the ultimate judgment and removal of corrupt worldly powers aligned against God
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:16 describes the ten horns turning against the harlot, symbolizing God's sovereign orchestration of judgment on corrupt powers as part of redemptive fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 17:11 and 17:8 teach about the beast's nature and destiny?
options: The beast is both a temporal manifestation of evil and destined for perdition
The beast is immortal and divine
The beast is a symbol for Christ's kingdom
The beast is eternal and unconquerable
questions.correctAnswer: The beast is both a temporal manifestation of evil and destined for perdition
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:8 and 17:11 together show the beast 'was, and is not' and is the eighth but of the seven, destined to go into perdition, emphasizing both its temporal existence and final destruction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 17:12 and 17:13 teach about the alliance of earthly powers with evil?
options: Ten kings will receive authority briefly to unite with the beast in opposition to God
Ten kings will establish a permanent righteous kingdom
The beast acts independently of earthly powers
The ten kings reject the beast and remain neutral
questions.correctAnswer: Ten kings will receive authority briefly to unite with the beast in opposition to God
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:12–13 depicts ten kings receiving power for one hour and giving their strength to the beast, indicating a temporary but unified opposition to God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 17:4 and 17:6 teach about the character of the great harlot and her opposition to the saints?
options: The harlot is adorned with worldly riches but is bloodthirsty toward the saints
The harlot is a humble servant of God
The harlot is unaware of her actions
The harlot protects the saints from harm
questions.correctAnswer: The harlot is adorned with worldly riches but is bloodthirsty toward the saints
questions.explanation: Verses 17:4 and 17:6 describe the woman arrayed in luxurious attire holding a cup of abominations and drunken with the blood of the saints, showing her corrupt nature and violent opposition to God's people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Revelation 17:8-11 teaches that the beast is an eternal evil power with no end. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The beast is a temporal entity destined for destruction
The beast is immortal and eternal
The beast is a myth with no real significance
questions.correctAnswer: The beast is a temporal entity destined for destruction
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:8-11 states the beast 'was, and is not,' will ascend from the bottomless pit, and go into perdition, clearly teaching its temporal existence and final destruction.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of evil's seduction does Revelation 17:15 teach?
options: Evil seduces diverse peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues
Evil is limited to a single ethnic group
Evil only affects the spiritual realm
Evil has no influence on human societies
questions.correctAnswer: Evil seduces diverse peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:15 explains the waters where the harlot sits represent peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues, symbolizing evil’s broad seduction across all humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic symbolism does Revelation 17:9 teach regarding the seven heads of the beast?
options: The seven heads represent seven mountains on which the woman sits
The seven heads are seven literal animals
The seven heads symbolize seven angels of God
The seven heads are unrelated to geography
questions.correctAnswer: The seven heads represent seven mountains on which the woman sits
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:9 explicitly states the seven heads are seven mountains, indicating symbolic prophetic geography often identified with Rome.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providential control over history is taught in Revelation 17:10?
options: There are seven kings with divinely ordained succession and timing
Kings rule by chance and human will alone
Kings have no impact on divine plans
The number seven is incidental without theological meaning
questions.correctAnswer: There are seven kings with divinely ordained succession and timing
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:10 describes seven kings with a specific sequence, indicating God’s providential ordering of history.

questions.question: What doctrine about the identity of 'the great city' does Revelation 17:18 teach?
options: The woman is the great city which reigns over the kings of the earth
The woman is a generic symbol without specific identity
The woman represents the heavenly Jerusalem
The woman is only a future city on earth
questions.correctAnswer: The woman is the great city which reigns over the kings of the earth
questions.explanation: Revelation 17:18 identifies the woman as 'that great city' which holds dominion over earthly kings, indicating her symbolic representation of worldly political and religious power.
